महोदय, खुदरा महंगाई में इजाफे के बाद मुद्रास्फीति बीस महीनों में सबसे ऊंचाई पर है। थोक महंगाई पर भी उसी तरह से ऊंचाई पर पहुंच चुकी है। सरकार को चिंता है या नहीं, लेकिन मैं समझता हूं कि देश की जनता को जरूर चिंता है कि खाद्य पदार्थों की इसी तरह से अगर कीमतें बढ़ती रहीं तो वह आखिर किस तरह से अपने बाल-बच्चों का पेट भरेंगे। उनके सामने यह एक बहुत बड़ा सवाल है। महंगाई की दर आज 7.88 प्रतिशत तक पहुंच गई है, जो 23 महीने के उच्चतम स्तर पर है। दो साल में अरहर की दाल की कीमत दोगुनी हो चुकी है, उड़द की दाल की कीमत 120 फीसदी बढ़ गई है। उसी तरह सब्जियों में टमाटर, प्याज और हर तरह की हरी सब्जियों की कीमतें आसमान छू रही हैं। 

उपाध्यक्ष महोदय, अब तक महंगाई का जो बोझ होता था, वह शहरों में रहने वाले लोगों पर ज्यादा होता था। लेकिन अभी यह देखा जा रहा है कि शहरों से ज्यादा गांवों में महंगाई बढ़ी है। जबकि ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों के लोगों की आमदनी कम होती है, उनके पास साधन कम होते हैं, लेकिन उन्हें भी इस महंगाई का बोझ झेलना पड़ रहा है, यह बहुत ही चिंता का विषय है। सरकार कहती है कि जमाखोरों के खिलाफ कड़ी कार्रवाई हो रही है। एक तरफ यह बात कही जाती है और दावा किया जाता है कि हम उनके खिलाफ कार्रवाई कर रहे हैं, छापे मारे जा रहे हैं। लेकिन दूसरी तरफ जो बिचौलिये हैं, जो जमाखोर हैं, उन्हें देखकर ऐसा लगता है कि उन्हें किसी बात का डर नहीं है, किसी बात का खौफ नहीं है। एक तरफ मंत्री समूह की बैठक होती है, कैबिनेट सचिव बैठक बुलाते हैं, प्रधान मंत्री जी का निर्देश भी आता है, परंतु इन सबके बावजूद कहीं भी जमाखोरी कम नहीं होती है। 

महोदय, यह बात समझ में आती है कि हमारे देश में दाल, दलहन का उत्पादन कम हुआ है। लेकिन आप जब बाजार में जाएं और उसकी दोगुनी और तिगुनी कीमत दें तो आपको वह दाल मिल जाती है, वह दलहन मिल जाता है, आपको सारी चीजें मुहैय्या हो जाती हैं। लेकिन अगर आप उसे सही दाम पर हासिल करना चाहें तो वह नहीं मिलती है। आखिर यह जो व्यवस्था है, यह बीच में जो एक गैप है, यह सरकार उसे कैसे पूरा करेगी और उन मुनाफाखोरों के खिलाफ कार्रवाई करेगी। ऐसा लगता है कि मुनाफाखोर यह मानकर चल रहे हैं कि इस सरकार में उनका कुछ भी बिगड़ने वाला नहीं है। इसलिए मनमाने ढंग से वे अपना काम कर रहे हैं और उसमें कोई रुकावट नहीं आ रही है। 

मैं कहना चाहता हूं कि सरकार की नींद तब टूटती हैं, जब महंगाई बढ़ जाती है। हम मंत्री जी से जानना चाहते हैं कि लगभग हर वर्ष यह बात उठती है, कीमतें बढ़ती हैं, जो अलग-अलग सामग्री हैं, उनकी कीमतें बढ़ती हैं। उसके लिए सरकार पहले से कोई उपाय क्यों नहीं करती है, पहले से उसके लिए व्यवस्था क्यों नहीं करती है। जब हाहाकार होने लगता है, जब लोग परेशान हो जाते हैं, जब लोगों की जेबों से पैसा निकाल लिया जाता है, तभी जाकर सरकार की आंखें खुलती हैं। फिर बाहर से सामग्री का निर्यात किया जाता है और यह कहा जाता है कि हम अपना स्टाक बढ़ाने जा रहे हैं, आने वाले दिनों में महंगाई कम होगी और जब नई पैदावार आएगी, तब महंगाई कम होगी, इस तरह के आश्वासन दिये जाते हैं और लोग परेशानियों का सामना करते रहते हैं। यह सरकार की लापरवाही नहीं तो और क्या है, यह हमें साफ तौर पर दिखाई पड़ रहा है। 

अंत में मैं इतना ही कहूंगा कि अगर सही मायनों में यह सरकार महंगाई पर नियंत्रण करने को लेकर गंभीर है तो उसे सही उपाय करने होंगे। आंकड़े देकर लोगों की परेशानियों को दूर नहीं किया जा सकता है। साधारण भा­षा में यही कहा जा सकता है कि अगर सरकार को सही मायनों में अपने पुराने वायदे याद हैं तो उन्हें पूरा करने के लिए उसे ठोस कदम उठाने की जरूरत है। 

आखिर में मैं अपनी बात उर्दू की इस पंक्ति के साथ खत्ना करना चाहता हूं - 

“मुद्दत हो गई कोई शख्स तो अब ऐसा मिले,

बाहर से जो दिखता हो, अंदर से भी वैसा ही दिखे।”

इन्हीं शब्दों के साथ मैं अपनी बात समाप्त करता हूं। धन्यवाद।

*SHRIMATI BUTTA RENUKA (KURNOOL): I express my views on this important subject concerning the entire country especially backward areas like my constituency.

The recent price rise in the essential commodities is of very serious concern as it is hurting the common man. The prices of onion, tomatoes, and pulses have seen an abnormal rise, going beyond the reach of the lower and middle class sections of the society. Since they are essential one cannot avoid buying them at whatever cost. This is mainly because there is no supportive government policy which could have helped to raise the pulses production by giving more incentives to the farmers growing onions, tomatoes and pulses. It is also necessary to provide warehousing facilities including cold storage so as to maintain near to uniform prices throughout the year. Further successive governments have failed to foresee demand and supply and take appropriate measures beforehand. It is not that the farmer is benefitted out of the price rise. It is only the middlemen, hoarders and retailers who are having the profit margin of more than 50% and the farmers are not reasonably rewarded for their labour. These middlemen are speculating and holding the common man to ransom. 

Another major reason for the prevailing high prices is the policy of the government in not passing on the benefits of reduced crude prices to the ultimate consumers. Whenever there is increase in crude oil prices at the global level the retail prices of petrol and diesel are automatically raised. However when there is fall in global oil prices the entire benefit is not passed on resulting in high petrol and diesel prices. This is having a serious impact on the essential commodity prices because of high transportation costs.

Another reason for increase in prices is the rise in the cost of inputs like seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and labour costs. Because of this, the farmers are at losing end and many of them, unable to survive are migrating to urban areas in search of livelihood and are converting themselves into urban labour. This is a dangerous trend as it will have serious repercussions on agricultural production and will have cascading effect on the prices of essential commodities.

I represent a constituency which is a major producer of tomatoes and onions. In any given year, the lows and highs of these products are more than 10 fold. The price of tomatoes vary from Rs. 2 per kg to Rs. 60 per kg. I have personally seen and consoled the families when the farmers have thrown their produce on the road as the price does not even cover the transportation costs.When the price goes up the farmer does not have the product with him.

The main beneficiaries of this would be the speculators, hoarders, middlemen, and the farmer is the victim. If proper storage facilities are developed the price can be maintained at a reasonable level benefitting the farmer and the consumer. Rising prices encourage hoarding, black-marketing and corruption.

It is a dangerous trend that farmers are not very keen on taking up cultivation of pulses, onions and tomatoes due to high fluctuations in production and prices. There is no minimum support price mechanism. Because of this, farmers are switching over to cash crops, because of better return and lower risk.

I understand that in a growing economy like ours inflation is a necessary evil. I appreciate the measures being taken by the Hon'ble Finance Minister in containing inflation without compromising on economic growth.

In spite of the best efforts of the Government the problem continues to be very serious and dangerous. It requires stern and effective measures.

The measures include improving our farm infrastructure like setting up of warehouses, cold-storage units etc. I also strongly recommend that support prices can be announced for farm produce like dal, onions and tomatoes. Stern action shall be taken against hoarders and middle men. Proper marketing facilities shall be developed which will ensure removal of middle men so that the farmers can get reasonable price for their products.

Agriculture is our backbone and farmer and agricultural labour are pillars to our economy and let us not allow a situation where the farmers and agricultural labour are depressed of their occupation and are moving to urban areas in search of livelihood.

* SHRI PRASANNA KUMAR PATASANI (BHUBANESWAR): This is one topic on which I do not have to think before placing in the House. The recent price rise in the essential commodities has hurt the common man, where it hurts the most. The prices of onion, tomatoes, pulses have skyrocketed which adds flavor to the otherwise normal lifestyle of below average Indian. The above statement is a sarcasm in itself, but it is necessary to show the grave situation which the normal citizens of this country are facing in the normal time.

The price of pulses which is nearly a staple diet for most of the country has risen to a large extent from the last 2 years. This may be due to less area under production for pulses in country or less per hectare yield of pulses or growth in demand. But the apathy is that there is no supportive government policy which could have helped India to raise the pulses production by giving more incentives to the farmers growing pulses, reducing loses to the intermediaries. One more benefit of higher pulses production is that it takes less of nitrogenous fertilizers and is essential for regular wheat/rice fields.

The prices of onion has risen nearly 300% or more in the last month. The first reason is inefficient government policy which do not foresee demand- supply situations, since onions are perishable quantities. The recent unseasonal rains in Nasik area has destroyed 10% of the crops, but still the quantum of price rise cannot be substantiated. The major culprit here is that there is no control over the last leg of supply chain i.e. retailers, who are having the profit margin of more than 50%. They are speculating on the deficient supply and holding the common man at ransom. Moreover in India export was stopped at a much later stage, which led to the spike in prices in the first instance. The rest and the last reason which is common to all, I would discuss in the later part.

There is another factor which is at play in high inflation rates across the commodities and it is ever increasing rates of petrol and diesel. The common plea given by the government to the people of India during every rate increase is the rising international crude prices. But they should first answer why there is double taxation by Center and the States on sale of petrol and diesel. My first question to the respective governments is why cannot these duties be reduced, so that atleast the transportation cost for the common commodities is reduced.

Now let us come to the contentious issue which is common to all the commodities price rise and bone of contention between the government and opposition parties, that is forward trading. Now some people will criticize me of knowing very little of the commodity trading, but my only point is why do you need speculative trading on the essential commodities, when you could have such trading on nearly each and every finance vehicle like equity shares, currency exchanges, etc. The forward trading increases the speculation in markets and people who are really not in the supply chain of these commodities get into it and unnecessarily disrupts the chain leading to disparity in normal price mechanism of the commodities.

Similarly, prices of milk and other commodities could be discussed singly, but I just want to make a point that a concerted serious action is required for dealing with the situation as it is hurting the foundation of common man economics in India. All the arms of government machinery, NGO’s common man should make an effort to discuss this problem and devise solutions which are practical and pragmatic in nature. Well, I am doing my part by writing and publishing this article on net, so that our online community is more educated on the topic which is raging in India currently.

Price hike in essential commodities has been a norm in our country. The pattern is very frequent, for instance, the petrol prices have been hiked ten times in the last 6 years. The hikes have become a nightmare for the “aam aadmi”. The ever increasing cost of living has once again proven the age old theory of Survival of the Fittest.

Interestingly, we discover an array of exciting facts when we dig in the depths of the issue. It is quite a common phenomenon that when the prices get hiked, substantial control measures have to be employed to check it. Paradoxically, government has seldom made efforts to curb it as it considers hike a part of the game.

Recently, in the President’s address, it was quoted that “higher prices were inevitable”. Rather, it was made inevitable. Hike is a nice and easy tool for the government to fill in the gaps of revenue. Whenever, the government is in any kind of trouble, it makes us bear the burden. 

Petrol price hike is an epitome to show government’s incapability or lack of accountability. Though the international fuel prices have fallen sharply by almost 100% in 2009, the Indian government shows no signs of reducing the price in the domestic market. Petrol, diesel and other petroleum products have an enormous impact on almost all the other commodity prices.

Black markets also contribute massively to hike. Sugar prices prove to be a fitting example. The recent price rise of sugar seems to be a rat race with its sweetness. The profits of 33 sugar companies have rocketed by 2900% to 900 crores, along with a gigantic increase in the sugar prices. The reason being crop shortage which was in turn created due to uncontrolled exports last year. We could have built buffer stocks, when we had the bumper crop, but we didn’t. This facilitated a raise in profits of all the export and import companies, while consumers were forced to pay much more than what they need to pay for sugar.

The strategic failure of agricultural departments, which failed to create proper awareness among the farmers regarding selection of crops, which eventually lead to price rise of pulses, cereals and vegetables drastically. Standard of living of common man has been taken to the limit. In 2009, 13.6 million people freshly joined the list of BPL in our country, according to a report by U.N. Department of Economic and Social Affairs. The hikes have made the lives of people miserable, forcing them to cut on luxuries and lead an austere life. Government has eventually made people unhappy and provoking suicidal tendencies in many who are fed up with this continuous price rise.

Politicians have been pro-commercial rather than pro-people for they have eased this hike with their malign usage of political influence in economic interests. Government is trying to justify that the conditions have been similar throughout the world. But, a comparison of the consumer price index with the other G-20 nations shows that India has the highest consumer price inflation at 14.97%, making it evident that the domestic policies are responsible for this.

The need of the hour is to set up specifically dedicated departments to study the trends in economy, which analyse the exports, imports and domestic agriculture conditions and propose new policies to check the price hike in our country.

*DR. KULMANI SAMAL (JAGATSINGHPUR): I am grateful for the opportunity to participate in the discussion regarding rise in prices of essential commodities in the Country. 

I would like to mention that now the issue of price rise has been an important issue in every corner of the country. I would like to mention that when general election was fought in 2014, it was one of the important agenda on which the NDA Government made its manifesto. During Congress regime especially in 2012-13, price of essential commodities got increased at the rate of around 23%. However, during the regime of this NDA Government since 2014, it has increased at the rate of more than 70%. We all know that the rise in prices of essential commodities, such as rice, wheat, pulses, vegetables, sugar, etc. has skyrocketed. We know that one-fourth of the hunger-stricken people in the world today live in India. We are talking about digitalization, start up India, Make in India, internet, speed rails, many infrastructure projects but still we are not able to provide essential commodities to the people.

According to the latest study undertaken by ASSOCHAM, in the last two years, the prices of essential commodities have gone up by nearly 72 percent and on the contrary the per capita income have gone up by only 38 percent of average Indian in metros.

I would like to state that the demand as well as supply, both factors are responsible for rise in prices of essential commodities. Apart from increasing population which itself is a major cause of rising demand, changing food habits are also responsible for increasing inflation. On the supply side, it is known to all of us that unfavorable weather conditions also resulted in the short supply of commodities and consequently pushed their prices up. Lack of warehousing facilities, cold storages also results in the post harvest losses which are estimated to the tune of one-third of the total produce. An abnormally high percentage of fruits and vegetables go wasted because of lack of cold-storage facilities. Thus post harvest losses also contribute to the short supply of food crops. The sharp increase in prices of wheat and rice will have an inflationary impact on essential commodities as open market prices of both commodities were posing slightly higher than the above the poverty line prices. Many essential commodities like petroleum products, pulses, fertilizers are either imported or are produced with imported intermediate goods. Price of such commodities depends on the international prices and as overall global prices of these commodities is increasing, pressure on domestic prices is bound to happen. Even in the case of export based goods produced in the country, if international prices of such commodities are soaring, there is an upward pressure on domestic prices as well because the producers will tend to sell these products in foreign markets where they are likely to fetch better prices. It may also create scarcity in domestic market. Moreover, market is also dominated by manipulators, fixers, middlemen, corporate gamblers etc. 

The inflation can be controlled to the large extent if the government gives full freedom to farmers to sell their agricultural produce anywhere in India without any restriction and ensure free movement without taxing the same. All the agricultural produce is controlled by market forces which include hoarders, black marketers and other rich and traditional traders. The prices of goods are decided by these individuals. They create the artificial shortage and price rise. The farmers cannot sell their agriculture produce directly due to different reasons. The real farmers use to get 1/3rd of the price. Rest of the profit is swallowed by the middleman and traders only.

Thus, the price rise is caused by several factors like hoarding, population explosion, low productivity, natural calamities, backwardness of communication, evil motives of dishonest businessmen, smuggling, black marketing etc.

But to control such loopholes, a sincere political will is necessary which is visibly lacking in the present Government. That is why they are silent on the issue. So, it is my sincere suggestion that the Government should focus upon comprehensive reforms, development of agriculture infrastructure, elimination of hoarders and black marketers to eliminate the artificial scarcity plaguing the economy of the Country at present. I feel, it is necessary on part of the Government to meet the promise they made to the people during the general election in 2014. Thank you.

*SHRIMATI V. SATHYABAMA (TIRUPPUR): I express my sincere thanks and gratitude to our beloved leader HON'BLE CHIEF MINISTER PURATCHI THALAIVI AMMA for giving this opportunity to express my views on the price rise issue. 

The very sharp rise in prices of food and essential commodities was a phenomenon that characterized the last few years of the erstwhile UPA Government’s tenure in office, caused primarily due to the poor macroeconomic management of the then Government of India. Some of those inflationary trends have persisted in the present Government’s tenure as well. Though overall inflation has been kept under check, food inflation has not been effectively tackled. Some decisive action by the Government of India is essential to ensure that the common person is protected against rapid rise in prices, particularly of food and essential commodities.

In Tamil Nadu, the State Government under the capable and determined leadership of the Hon'ble Chief Minister, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma has taken a large number of appropriate measures to ensure that the common people and the poor and the vulnerable are protected against the rise in prices of essential commodities.

One of the first decisions of the Hon'ble Chief Minister Puratchi Thalaivi Amma on assumption of office in May, 2011 was to announce and implement the free supply of 20 kilogrammes of rice per month through the Public Distribution System to about 1.83 crore families in the State. Tamil Nadu’s PDS is the best
 functioning Public Distribution System in the country as recognized by many economists and scholars both in India and abroad. The supply of free rice in the PDS has greatly helped the vast majority of families in the State and protected them against the rise in food prices.

The well functioning Public Distribution System in Tamil Nadu has also been effectively leveraged by the State Government to reach other essential commodities to the people of the State at reasonable prices. 1 litre of refined palm oil is supplied at Rs 25 and 1 kilogram each of urad and toor dhal are supplied at Rs. 30 per kg to all family card holders as part of the Special Public Distribution System. The State Government incurs an expenditure of Rs.1861 crores on the Special PDS out of its own budgetary resources every year.

The steep rise of prices of vegetables and pulses is a very serious concern in Indian homes in recent months. It has made the life of common people, poor and middle class in particular miserable. The price of pulses and other essential commodities including the petroleum products have reached an unreachable maximum. The sky-rocketing prices of vegetables and pulses have made any average middle class family think twice before buying or consuming them. The big question is why is there constant food inflation?

Frequent Fuel price rises affect the prices of all other essential commodities dearly. HON'BLE CHIEF MINISTER PURATCHI THALAIVI AMMA has opposed the frequent revision in fuel prices that too when the international price of crude oil is down to all time low in last 10 years. The Hon'ble Prime Minister should intervene and make necessary efforts to have a price control and regulation policy to put brakes to such consistent hike. The Centre is getting revenue by revising excise duty, but passing the burden on he common man was “an unjust act”. People of South India, rich or poor, thrive mainly on idly-vada-dosa-sambar as their staple food and quite naturally depends on pulses and grains. People of Tamil Nadu who consumes larger quantities of various types of pulses, are the most affected due to the sky-rocketing prices of vegetables and pulses in the recent times.

In an attempt to stabilize the soaring prices of pulses and augment its availability, the Tamil Nadu government under the dynamic leadership of HON'BLE CHIEF MINISTER PURATCHI THALAIVI AMMA have ordered to sell 500 metric tonnes of toor dal in its cooperative outlets at subsidized rates (Half a kg of toor dal is priced at Rs. 55, and a kg at Rs. 110). The imported dal is being sold through 36 outlets run by TUCS, North Chennai, Chintamani cooperative societies and 20 Amudham departmental stores and is available in 11 cooperative outlets in Madurai, 14 in Tiruchirapalli and 10 in Coimbatore. The PDS outlets would continue to sell the subsidized toor dal (Canadian yellow lentils), urad dal and palm oil at Rs. 30 and Rs. 25 respectively. “These timely initiatives would help stabilize the market rate of toor dal,”. It is because of efforts made by HON'BLE CHIEF MINISTER PURATCHI THALAIVI AMMA the ill effects of price rise on the poor and middle class people have been reduced considerably.

Since with the change in eating habits, many families consume pulses in excess of what is supplied to Special PDS each month, which they purchase in the open market, in order to moderate the increases in prices of dhall in the open market. The Government of Tamil Nadu has also lunched a Market Stabilisation Fund with a provision of Rs. 100 crores for effective market intervention through the co-operative wholesale stores network to moderate the prices of dal in the State. A total of 230 tonnes of urad dhal and 120 tonnes of toor dal were supplied through this mechanism which helped to substantially bring down market prices, effectively curbing the hoarding tendency through market means.

Tamil Nadu’s Universal Public Distribution System, commended both within India and elsewhere, is a model food security programme. This is a vital programme, which requires constant vigil and monitoring so as to ensure that the benefits continue to reach the deserving persons and to plug leakages. HON'BLE CHIEF MINISTER PURATCHI THALAIVI AMMA has ordered the officials to ensure that the process of collection of bio-metric information through the National Population Register is expedited and the State is in a position to issue smart cards to all families in the State at the earliest.

The Government of Tamil Nadu under the leadership of Hon'ble Chief Minister Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA has also launched several initiatives to make available fresh vegetables to consumers in urban areas, while at the same time ensuring that vegetables farmers get remunerative prices. As part of the many measures taken by this Government to combat price rise, 48 Farm Fresh Vegetable Outlets have been opened in Chennai. Consumers are now able to buy vegetables at reasonable prices and at the same time farmers get both an assured market and remunerative prices. Already, 2482 metric tonnes of vegetables valued at 7.38 crore rupees have been sold through these Outlets. To ensure sustainable vegetable supply, 10,493 farmers have been provided crop loans of 55.22 crore rupees for the cultivation of vegetables. AMMA had instructed the District Collectors to open Farm Fresh Outlets at appropriate locations in their Districts for the benefit of the public.

Why the prices of pulses, vegetables and other essential commodities are increasing continuously in India? It is not only due to a poor harvest or due to a bad monsoon. There are 10 important man-made reasons which results in the rising prices of commodities.

1. Global inflation

2. Less space for cultivation

3. Less production of pulses

4. Increased cost of production

5. Improper management and distribution

6. Fuel price rise and increased cost of transportation

7. Hoarding

8. Many mediators 

9. Supply chain mismanagement and

10. Increased demand for protein-enriched food and green vegetables

It is unfortunate to see, India’s villages face a sharp spike in food prices in 2016, as a second year of drought drives up the cost of ingredients such as sugar and milk, and poor transport infrastructure stops falling global prices from reaching rural areas. While urban dwellers have seen some cheaper imported food products, benefitting from global deflation, that has not filtered through to rural areas, given poor roads, rail and a lack of storage facilities for perishable goods. Prices of vegetables like onions, tomatoes and potatoes have already been rising. Palm oil prices have also climbed in the last two months, while milk prices have risen by 1- per cent. Edible oil prices in India, which meets nearly 70 per cent of demand through imports, are also likely to rise, given scant rainfall in palm oil-producing countries. Meanwhile, scarcity of fodder and water is expected to hit local milk production. The less production will obviously allow prices to rise. The rural economy contributes around 50 per cent of Indian gross domestic product and is already showing signs of strain as government cuts the once-generous subsidies that shielded farmers and villagers. Agriculturists income dropped nearly 50 percent due to drought. They borrowed loan from banks for seeds and fertilizer, but now they don’t know how to repay the loan. 

Continuing the past trend of significant increases in the minimum support price of pulses, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs raised those of masoor (red gram) and gram (Bengal gram), the two most sown in the rabi season, by Rs. 250 a quintal. A bonus of Rs. 75 a quintal has also been recommended over and above the MSP, a total increase of Rs. 325 a quintal as compared to 2014-15.

Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs also authorized Food Corporation of India, along with other procuring agencies, to undertake procurement of pulses and oilseeds. The MSP of wheat, the biggest rabi food grain, has been raised by Rs. 75 a quintal, highest increase in recent years. If the money we spend on importing pulses reaches our farmers, there won’t be any suicides or shortage of food grains. There has been an overall increase in the prices of almost every commodity.

Just as onions left many crying, it is now the turn of pulses (dal). The price of the poor man’s staple has doubled and there is no visible measures to check its spiraling growth. While India has reached self-sufficiency in many food items, which includes milk, rice and wheat, it has not been able to do the same with pulses. While all these revolutions had their own god fathers like Varghese Kurien or M S Swaminathan, pulses, one of the most used ingredients in the Indian kitchen had not found support from any quarter. Approximately, an annual import bill of $2.6 billion is incurred by India only on pulses. If this amount were to reach our farmers, they may never think of leaving farming – leave alone committing suicide. Lack of policies or clarity on agriculture planning has led to this crisis which is not going to abate in the near future.

As a rule, the demand for all commodities reaches a peak during the festival season in India. Pulses are no exception. India is facing a crisis because of deficient rainfall at one end and excess rainfall at the other side. But we cannot blame this alone for this crisis. Crisis is mainly in tur and urad dals, two of the most consumed pulses, as total pulses’ production dipped to 17.2 million tonnes last year against 19.25 million tonnes in the previous year. Domestic production may be just 17 MT against the demand of 27 MT. Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh are the major pulses-producing regions followed by Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Canada, Ukraine, the US, Australia, Myanmar and a few African countries contribute to India’s pulses need.

Pulses production in India has been showing less than 40 per cent growth during the last 5 decades and this has led to almost halving the per capital availability to 30 grams now. So this precisely means the prices are doubling at an alarmingly low periodicity. We also have to take stock of the Green Revolution and what it has achieved. Though we are self-sufficient in rice and wheat, crop rotation has made the soil of some of the northern states, unfit for use. The result is there for all to see. But crop rotation and diversification could have helped retain the soil. But we never put other essential commodities in this agriculture cycle and the net result is that the farmers of Canada, Myanmar and Australia are benefitting instead of our own.

Approximately, India’s annual import bill of pulses alone is $2.6 billion. Imagine this reaching our own farmers, they may never think of leaving farming – leave alone think of committing suicide. Just see the granaries of public distribution system like Food Corporation of India warehouses. Wheat and rice are rotting because we are over-producing both. Why can’t we replace one of these with pulses? The question is, who will the farmers go to if something goes wrong with these decisions?

It is not that we cannot incentivize the production of pulse. There are many ways to do it and India’s climate is suited to grow most of the lentils we consume. The Minimum Support Price is also not transparent and depends on various political factors. Some of the lentils do come under MSP but they are not attractive enough for farmers to concentrate merely on pulses. Not all pulses come under the ambit of MSP. But more than MSP, it is procurement guarantee that matters.

To feed our growing population we need at least 30 million tonnes of lentils by 2030 which is close to five per cent growth annually. We are no way near. So we will continue to burn our foreign exchange reserves forever. By merely checking the prices of pulses, inflation is not going to be under control. There has been an overall increase in the prices of almost every commodity. People are now destined to live with it. It looks like the government should go by correct advice and take correct economic action on the ground.

Inflation in India generally occurs as a consequence of global traded commodities and the several efforts made by The Reserve Bank of India to weaken rupee against dollar. This has been regarded as the root cause of inflation crisis rather than the domestic inflation. According to some experts, the policy of RBI to absorb all dollars coming into the Indian Economy contributes to the appreciation of the rupee. When the US dollar has shrieked by a margin of 30%, Reserve Bank of India had made a massive injection of dollar in the economy make it highly liquid and this further triggered off inflation in non-traded goods.

The Amma Canteen scheme, a brain child of the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Puratchi Thalaivi Amma, which is now renowned across the world and studied by governments and experts from different parts of India and the world, has also had a salutary impact on keeping a check on food prices in Tamil Nadu. In Amma Canteens, idlis with sambar is supplied at Rs. 1 and curd rice at Rs. 3 and sambar rice at Rs. 5.

There are a number of other commodities which are also supplied at reasonable prices in Tamil Nadu. I would specifically like to highlight the Amma Mineral Water, Amma Salt, and Amma Cement programmes which ensure availability at reasonable prices of commodities prone to price increase due to cartelization and other factors. These interventions have had a salutary effect on market prices of such commodities. VAT on domestic LPG has also been completely exempted to ensure that price of domestic LPG is kept reasonable in spite of deregulation of LPG prices. 

Through many such innovative and imaginative schemes, the Government of Tamil Nadu under the leadership of the Hon'ble Chief Minister, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma has managed to ensure that the common people in the State have been protected against the ill-effects of price rise. This is no mean achievement.

Our leader, the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma has rightly cautioned against the implementation of the Direct Benefit Transfer scheme in areas where the availability and price level of commodities is a key concern. These are primarily the food, fertilizer, LPG and kerosene subsidy schemes, where the availability of the essential commodities and affordable prices is the key concern and merely transferring the monetary equivalent of the subsidy being incurred and that too on a pre-determined and fixed basis, will not adequately protect the food and nutritional security of the common people. Such a scheme would expose the common people who depend on the Public Distribution System and fertilizer supply to the vagaries of the market and deprive them of essential commodities. Hence, the Government of India should exercise the greatest care and caution in expanding the scope of the Direct Benefit Transfer scheme beyond those schemes which currently involve a cash transfer at present, like scholarships and pensions. This is the unequivocal stance of the AIADMK Party.

What can the Government of India do to bring down prices and protect the poor?

1. Subsidize food items including pulses and edible oil.

2. Roll back the additional excise duty levied on Petrol and Diesel announced earlier this year.

3. Enable cheaper movement by rail by reducing the freight rates of essential commodities.

4. Reduce the toll fee collected, particularly from freight vehicles.

5. Provide adequate input subsidy to farmers to encourage production of pulses and oil seeds with assured price and purchase mechanism.

All these factors have to be taken into account to control price rise in India. I urge upon the Union Government to take appropriate steps to control the soaring price rise graph and maintain the prices as lower as possible for the poor and middle class people of this country on the lines of HON'BLE CHIEF MINISTER PURATCHI THALAIVI AMMA.

*SHRI R. DHRUVANARAYANA (CHAMARAJANAGAR) : The GDP is expected to rise; there are claims of a lot of foreign investment being brought into our country, various schemes like Make in India, Start up India, etc. are being promoted. *डॉ. सुनील बलीराम गायकवाड़ (लातूर)ः जब 16 वीं लोक सभा के नतीजे आए और आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदीजी की नई सरकार बनी लेकिन " महंगाई " पूर्व सरकार ने बढ़ाकर ही सत्ता दे दी । इतनी बुरी हालत में भी जो महंगाई बढ़ी थी उस महंगाई को माननीय नरेंद्र मोदी जी की सरकार ने कंट्रोल में किया । तेलों के दाम डीजल, पेट्रोल की महंगाई आसमान को छू गई थी । जबकि आवश्यक वस्तु के दाम भी बहुत बढ़ चुके थे । लेकिन हमारी सरकार ने विभिन्न आवश्यक वस्तुओं के दाम कंट्रोल में लाकर आम जनता के हित में काम किया है । कुछ सब्जियां एवं तूर दाल की बातें यहां पर कही हो गई है। हमारे देश में भारत के विभिन्न जगहों पर बारीश ठीक तरह से नहीं हो पाई । इस हालत में भी मूल्य वृद्धि नहीं की गई । गरीबों के मदद की यह सरकार है । जो काम पिछले साठ साल में कांग्रेस की सरकार भी नहीं किया वह काम हमारे मोदीजी की सरकार ने दो साल में पूरा करके दिखाया है । इस अकाल की स्थिति में पहली बार हुआ है कि मराठवाड़ा-महाराष्ट्र में जो बारिश नहीं होने के कारण मुआवजा बड़ी मात्रा में किसानों के डायरेक्ट अकाउंट में जमा हुआ है । मार्केट में जैसे मांस का उत्पादन होगा वैसे ही उसकी कीमतों पर असर होता है । यह गरीबों की, दलितों की व्यापारियों की हित में काम करने वाली सरकार है ।

*SHRI S.P. MUDDAHANUME GOWDA (TUMKUR): The retail inflation is at 21-month high. The food inflation is up by 7.5 per cent. The vegetable prices are up. The prices of pulses are up by 30, 40 and 50 per cent. The prices of eggs, meat and fish are up. The only silver lining here is that if we look at it closely, all the prices are up. It is even worst today to be a vegetarian in India, than a non-vegetarian because comparatively meat and fish are more in control.

My second point is that the crude oil price which was 110 dollar per barrel, has come down to 45 to 47 dollar per barrel. There are six, seven countries where the price of petrol has come down, and the maximum price rise has been from five to ten per cent. In India, this is the worst example. In spite of this, those benefits are not being passed on to the consumers because, on the one side, they say, achhe din, but achhe din are not for the larger percentage of the population. The benefit should have been passed on to the people. Actually the petty reductions rarely announced by oil companies are nothing in comparison to the periodic increase in price effected by these companies. The Government of India also rubs salt to the festering wounds with increase in excise duties. Due to this, actually in the last two years, when the prices started coming down, there has been increase in the price of diesel and petrol. 

The ever increasing price rise affects all the poor and middle classes and also affects more to those who live in rural India. In the last 24 months up to June 2016, while urban inflation fell from 9 per cent to 5.3 per cent, rural inflation declined from 10.1 per cent to 6.2 per cent. In the fiscal 2016, rural core inflation was 6.7 per cent as compared to 4.8 per cent in urban. Sub-categories such as health, education, household goods and services and recreation and amusement have all recorded higher inflation in the rural areas last fiscal.

What can the Government of India do to bring down the prices and to protect the poor? It can subsidize the food items, including pulses and edible oil. It can roll back the additional excise duty levied on petrol and diesel announced earlier this year. Then, the Government can enable cheaper movement by rail by reducing the freight rates for essential commodities and by reducing the toll collected from private vehicles. The Government of India has announced that it intends to double the income of the agriculturists by 2022. In that case, it should provide adequate input subsidy to farmers to encourage production of pulses and oilseeds with assured price and purchase mechanism. They have now announced the Minimum Support Price for paddy and other commodities. But why is the Government ignoring the coconut farmers. The Government does not recognize them at all. 

Around four years back, the Minimum Support Price for copra was Rs. 53.50. In the long run of these four years, it has only increased by six rupees, that is, two plus four, and, accordingly, Rs. 59.50 has been fixed as the Minimum Support Price. Also, they are not getting the Minimum Support Price because of the norms prescribed. For example, it says that the moisture content must be below six per cent. It is very difficult to supply the same at six per cent moisture. Therefore, I want to request the Government that the procurement norms must be made liberal, and, it must be made 7.5 per cent. That would be the best thing. Another thing is that they can buy the de-husk coconuts directly at twenty four rupees a kilo, which will also satisfy the coconut farmers a little bit. Actually, the coconut farmers are demanding Rs. 100/- per kilo. If Rs. 100/- is not given, at least, it must be made Rs. 75/- per kilo, and, it must be procured by the Government. This is the position of today. Actually, the price of DAP, the price of potash as also the price of NPK complex fertilizer has gone up. So, the Government must be liberal in giving the Minimum Support Price for all the farm produce.

The leakages and inefficiencies in the food management system and inadequate supply chain management have also led to the price spiral and are also responsible for the recent spurt. The MSP policy, which was highly skewed in favour of rice and wheat, has discouraged the other key items leading to shortfall in their production.

Another point is that hoarding and speculative activities by the middlemen have created artificial scarcity in some commodities. The benefit of high prices paid by consumers does not flow back to primary producers, that is, farmers. But it is siphoned away by middlemen and speculators who enjoy a free run in an economy of shortages.

The infrastructure for post-harvest management of farm products to ensure proper storage and smooth supply to market is quite weak in our country. India is world’s largest producer of fruits and vegetables. But the shortage and transportation losses for several crops are estimated to be around 30-40 per cent. Unfortunately, there is no silver lining in sight.

Efficient market infrastructure, improved storage capacity and faster transportation from producers to customers are the vital areas that need greater attention. The transformation of agriculture has to be steered by raising productivity in agriculture by investing in efficient irrigation technology. It is equally important to gradually move away from the cereal-centric MSP policy towards other items with supportive policy framework and required infrastructure. Policy interventions are required to support sustainable growth in crop production and environmental protection through development of improved and diversified cultivation, eco-friendly and cost-effective pest management practices and efficient seed supply systems. I urge upon the Union Government to take immediate steps to control the prices of essential commodities for the benefit of the poor people of the country. Thank you.

SHRI JAYADEV GALLA (GUNTUR): Thank you, Sir, for giving me this opportunity to speak on this very important issue which has greatly disturbed mainly the kitchen of all the common men in the country.

Sitting here in the middle in no man’s land, I have been listening to the debate with a lot of disappointment, I must say. Both sides seem to be only concerned about trading charges, avoiding accountability and blaming each other for the current state of affairs. We are being given history lessons viewed through two very different lenses. It needs to be a more constructive dialogue focused on finding solutions rather than finding the guilty party. It is not a trial, Sir, to determine who is guilty and who is not but it is a dialogue where we have to look for robust and constructive solutions.

There was no doubt that we will either be discussing drought or floods or agrarian crisis or price rise in every Session. In this 16th Lok Sabha this is the third time we are speaking on the subject but we still do not seem to be finding the way forward.

Sir, when the farmer is in crisis, all poor people in the country will be in crisis. The country cannot prosper while the farmers are in crisis. We need to find durable and sustainable solutions. I had also participated last time when the issue was discussed and gave some suggestions to the Government but I do not know where those suggestions have gone. There is no doubt that we are part of the NDA but it does not stop me from ventilating the voice and concerns of the people who are really reeling with unprecedented rise in prices of essential commodities.

If you look at the statistics, on the one hand inflation has come down to half of what it used to be, fiscal deficit has narrowed by a third. The current account deficit has gone down from five per cent of GDP in 2013 to just one per cent of GDP in 2016. Foreign exchange reserves are a record high. This is one side of the picture. On the other side, industrial growth is not so encouraging. Retail inflation or Consumer Price Index has gone up to 5.77 per cent, which is the highest in the last 22 months. Of course, we all should agree that this is half of what it used to be in November, 2013. It was 11.16 per cent in 2013. The other things are not pinching the common man. I am not denying the fact that the Government is taking steps. It is taking the necessary steps but since the outcome is not visible to people in the form of reduced prices, naturally there will be agitation outside and fear inside this House, Sir.

I am told that the Competition Commission initiated an inquiry but it is immaterial for the people whether the Competition Commission has initiated inquiry behind the sudden surge in prices or the Government is importing pulses for seasonal variation between demand and supply. People want their basic and essential commodities at affordable prices. That is the bottom line.

The main problem with regard to pulses is that we are able to produce 16-17 million tonnes but the demand is 24-25 million tonnes and the gap needs to be filled through imports. For example, pulses output declined to 17.15 million metric tonnes in 2014-15 from 19 million metric tonnes in the previous year. Last year there was a further dip to 17 million metric tonnes when the domestic demand is 24 million tonnes. So, I strongly feel that the supply side factors such as inadequacy of agricultural output in proportion to the population, inadequacy of industrial output due to various factors, including global slow down and high priced inputs are influencing the price level of various commodities.

Last time when I spoke during the Discussion on Price Rise I had made some suggestions for the consideration of the Government. I understand that the Government has not acted on them. So, even if this is a repetition, I wish to reiterate and request the Government to at least give a thought to these suggestions.

The Food Security Act emphasises rice and wheat and not giving any place for pulses. Had pulses been included in the Food Security Act we would have been achieving the twin objectives of giving the much needed proteins to the poor people and also increasing the production and productivity of pulses. 

The second point is that we are not giving priority to pulses in MSP. They are always graded next to cereals. This is affecting the production and productivity. Let me substantiate my point. Sir, production of foodgrains in 1950-51 was 50.85 million tonnes and now it has gone up to around 270 million tonnes thanks to the Green Revolution. It means, there is more than five times increase in the production of foodgrains. When it comes to pulses, the production was 8.41 million tonnes in 1950-51 and today the production is about 17 million tonnes. If you look at the productivity of pulses when compared to other countries and world average, we are lagging far behind. Our productivity is 694 kilograms per hectare, China has 1567 kilograms per hectare which is almost three times our productivity. Even Pakistan has 762 kilograms per hectare and Nepal with 791 kilograms per hectares. They are ahead of us. These two examples will give enough indication of the importance that we are giving or not giving to pulses. I am not repeating here the other suggestions made by me last time to increase productivity and production of pulses as they are already there with the hon. Minister and I am limited by the time. 

In 2010-11 Budget the Government had started BGREI i.e., Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India. It has brought very good results and the food grain production in the Eastern India has gone up by 15 per cent when compared to all-India production growth of only three per cent. Prime Minister, on the lines of Green Revolution, White Revolution and BGREI revolution. This will make our country self-sufficient in pulses if we are successful. 

I also welcome the Prime Minister’s Fasal Bima Yojana. It is a very good scheme started six months ago. I only suggest the hon. Minister - even though he is not concerned with this scheme - to convey to Agriculture Minister to take this scheme to every farmer of this country. 

Subsidies given to farmers are also important. If you look at the subsidies given by India and other countries, we are way behind at just 

2.3 per cent. USA is giving 26 per cent subsidy, China is giving 34 per cent, South Africa is giving 60 per cent subsidy. But we are just giving 2.3 per cent subsidy in spite of the fact that more than 60 per cent of our population depend on agricultural income. Sir, I am concluding. I just want to give a couple of points about my State. Secondly, under the able leadership of Shri Nara Chandrababu Naidu Garu, in spite of facing drought in the last two years, Andhra Pradesh distributes pulses through PDS. The Government of Andhra Pradesh, with an objective to deliver all welfare and development services directly to the beneficiaries and to eliminate middlemen and removing all fake and ineligible beneficiaries, has linked Aadhar and Jan-Dhan Yojana with Direct Benefit Transfer of several welfare and development programmes. Sir, these are suggestions which are very useful compared to the debate that we have been having so far. I will just take one or two more minutes. The other significant step that the Government of Andhra Pradesh has taken is that when the Government of India released 21,000 MT of Tur and Urad from buffer stock to States at subsidized rate of 120 per kilogram to stabilize the price of pulses, we are distributing Tur at a highly subsidized rate of Rs. 50 per kg through PDS in Andhra Pradesh.

These have to be changed.

Thank you once again.

*SHRI P. NAGARAJAN (COIMBATORE): I express my sincere gratitude and indebtedness to our beloved leader HON'BLE CHIEF MINISTER PURATCHI THALAIVI AMMA for giving this opportunity to express my views on the Price rise issue.

The steep rise of prices of vegetables and pulses is a very serious concern in Indian homes in recent months. It has made the life of common people, poor and middle class in particular miserable. The price of pulses and other essential commodities including the petroleum products have reached an unreachable maximum. The sky-rocketing prices of vegetables and pulses have made any average middle class family think twice before buying or consuming them. 

Through many innovative and imaginative schemes, the Government of Tamil Nadu under the leadership of the HON'BLE CHIEF MINISTER PURATCHI THALAIVI AMMA has managed to ensure that the common people in Tamil Nadu have been protected against the ill-effects of price rise. The Amma Canteen scheme, a brain child of the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Puratchi Thalaivi Amma, which is now renowned across the world and studied by governments and experts from different parts of India and the world, has also had a salutary impact in keeping a check on food prices in Tamil Nadu.

There are a number of other commodities which are also supplied at reasonable prices in Tamil Nadu. I would specifically like to highlight the Amma Mineral Water, Amma Salt, and Amma Cement programmes which ensure availability of commodities at reasonable prices, which are prone to price increase due to cartelization and other factors. These interventions have had a salutary effect on market prices of such commodities. VAT on domestic LPG has also been completely exempted to ensure that price of domestic LPG is kept reasonable in spite of deregulation of LPG prices.

It is unfortunate to see, India’s villages face a sharp spike in food prices in 2016, as a second year of drought drives up the cost of ingredients such as sugar and milk, and poor transport infrastructure stops falling global prices from reaching rural areas. While urban dwellers have seen some cheaper imported food products, benefiting from global deflation, but that has not filtered through to rural areas.

While India has reached self-sufficiency in many food items, which includes milk, rice and wheat, it has not been able to do the same with pulses. While all these revolutions had their own godfathers like Varghese Kurien or M S Swaminathan, pulses, one of the most used ingredients in Indian kitchen, had not found support from any quarter. Approximately, an annual import bill of $ 2.6 billion is incurred by India only on pulses. If this amount were to reach our farmers, they may never think of leaving farming – leave alone committing suicide. Lack of policies or clarity on agriculture planning has led to this crisis which is not going to abate in the near future.

We also have to take stock of the Green Revolution and what it has achieved. Though we are self-sufficient in rice and wheat, crop rotation has made the soil of some of the northern states, unfit for use. The result is there for all to see. But crop rotation and diversification could have helped retain the soil. But we never put other essential commodities in this agriculture cycle and the net result is that the farmers of Canada, Myanmar and Australia are benefitting instead of our own.

India’s annual import bill of pulses alone is $2.6 billion. Imagine this reaching our own farmers, they may never think of leaving farming – leave alone think of committing suicide. Just see the granaries of public distribution system like Food Corporation of India warehouses. Wheat and rice are rotting because we are over-producing both. Why can’t we replace one of these with pulses? The question is, who will the farmers go to if something goes wrong with these decisions?

It is not that we cannot incentivize the production of pulses. There are many ways to do it and India’s climate is suited to grow most of the lentils we consume. The Minimum Support Price is also not transparent and depends on various political factors. Some of the lentils do come under MSP but they are not attractive enough for farmers to concentrate merely on pulses. Not all pulses come under the ambit of MSP. But more than MSP, it is procurement guarantee that matters.

To feed our growing population, we need at least 30 million tonnes of lentils by 2030 which is close to five per cent growth annually. We are no way near. So we will continue to burn our foreign exchange reserves forever. By merely checking the prices of pulses, inflation is not going to be under control. There has been an overall increase in the prices of almost every commodity. People are now destined to live with it. it looks like the government should go by correct advise and take correct economic action on the ground.

Inflation in India generally occurs as a consequence of global traded commodities and the several efforts made by The Reserve Bank of India to weaken rupee against dollar. This has been regarded as the root cause of inflation crisis rather than the domestic inflation. According to some experts, the policy of RBI to absorb all dollars coming into the Indian Economy contributes to the appreciation of the rupee. When the US dollar has shrieked by a margin of 30%, Reserve Bank of India had made a massive injection of dollar in the economy make it highly liquid and this further triggered off inflation in non-traded goods.

It is not only due to a poor harvest or due a bad monsoon. There are 10 important man-made reasons which results in the rising prices of pulses, vegetables and other essential commodities.

It is unfortunate to see that India’s villages face a sharp spike in food prices in 2016, as a second year of drought drives up the cost of ingredients such as sugar and milk, and poor transport infrastructure stops falling global prices from reaching rural areas. While urban dwellers have seen some cheaper imported food products, benefiting from global deflation, that has not filtered through to rural areas, given poor roads, rail and a lack of storage facilities for perishable goods.

Tamil Nadu’s Universal Public Distribution System commended both within India and elsewhere is a model food security programme. This is a vital programme, which requires constant vigil and monitoring so as to ensure that the benefits continue to reach the deserving persons and to plug leakages. HON'BLE CHIEF MINISTER PURATCHI THALAIVI AMMA has ordered the officials to ensure that the process of collection of bio-metric information through the National Population Register is expedited and the State is in a position to issue smart cards to all families in the State at the earliest. 

As part of the many measures taken by this Government to combat price rise, Farm Fresh Consumer Outlets have been opened in Chennai. Consumers are now able to buy vegetables at reasonable prices and at the same time, farmers get both an assured market and remunerative prices. To ensure sustainable vegetable supply, 10,493 farmers have been provided crop loans of 55.22 crore rupees for the cultivation of vegetables. AMMA had instructed the District Collectors to open Farm Fresh Outlets at appropriate locations in their Districts for the benefit of the public.

To feed our growing population we need at least 30 million tonnes of lentils by 2030 which is close to five per cent growth annually. We are no way near. So we will continue to burn our foreign exchange reserves forever. By merely checking the prices of pulses, inflation is not going to be under control. There has been an overall increase in the prices of almost every commodity. People are now destined to live with it. It looks like to government should go by correct advise and take correct economic action on the ground.

All these factors have to be taken into account to control price rise in India. I urge upon the Union Government to take appropriate steps to control the soaring price rise graph and maintain the prices as lower as possible for the poor and middle class people of this country on the lines of HON'BLE CHIEF MINISTER PURATCHI THALAIVI AMMA. Thank you.

SHRI A.P. JITHENDER REDDY (MAHABUBNAGAR): Mr. Chairman Sir, thank you for giving me this opportunity to participate in the discussion on price rise. महोदय, मैं बहुत ही साधारण हिन्दी भा­षा में बोलना चाह रहा हूँ। 

अरुण जेटली जी इतनी अच्छी रोज़ी पिक्चर और भाषण दे गए। उन्होंने यह कहा कि जब यूपीए सरकार थी तो प्राइसेज़ बहुत ऊँचाई पर थे। आज जब एनडीए सरकार आई है, तो Consumer Index has come down to a very low level. मुझे महंगाई एक ही समय में मालूम पड़ती है, और एक्चुअली मैं सोचता हूँ कि पुरु­षों के बजाय लेडीज़ को इस विषय पर ज्यादा बोलना चाहिए। पहले मेरी बीवी आकर मुझे बोलती थी कि 50 हज़ार रुपये दो, मैं गंज पर जाकर सामान ले आती हूँ। थोड़े दिन के बाद अभी बोलने लगी कि 50 हज़ार रुपये मुझे कम पड़ते हैं, मुझे एक लाख रुपये दो। मैं पूछता हूँ कि 50 हज़ार रुपये तुम ले जाती थी, अभी क्या हो रहा है, क्यों एक लाख रुपये चाहिए? तो वह बोलती है कि ज़रा आप महंगाई की तरफ तो देखो। जो ऑइल से हम कुकिंग करते हैं, वह जो 10 रुपये लीटर था, वह 80 रुपये लीटर हो गया है। सब्ज़ी जो 10 रुपये किलोग्राम मिलती थी, वह अभी 50 रुपये किलो मिलती है। टमाटर जो दो रुपये किलो मिलता था, वह 100 रुपये तक आ गया है। इस तरीके से सभी चीज़ों पर प्राइस बढ़ गया है। इसलिए गृहिणी को मालूम है कि प्राइस राइज़ का मतलब क्या है और इस पर भाषण केवल वही दे सकते हैं। जिस तरीके से इनफ्लेशन बढ़ा मैं उसके बारे में बता रहा हूँ। हम तो ज्यादा मार्केट में नहीं जाते हैं। मेरा कैम्प ऑफिस भी महबूबनगर में है। वह पहले 20 हजार रुपये में चलता था, आज वे लोग 80 हजार रुपये मांगते हैं। मेरा जो सिक्यूरिटी है, उनका जो मैस बिल मैं पे कर रहा था, पहले 25 हज़ार रुपये मैं पे कर रहा था और आज वह 60-70 हज़ार रुपये हो गया है। केवल भाषणों में सॉफिस्टिकेटेड वर्ड्ज़ यूज़ करते हुए प्राइस राइज़ को कम नहीं किया जा सकता है, यह मेरा मानना है। 

आज मार्केट की स्थिति बहुत ही बुरी है। मैं समझता हूँ कि किसी भी तरीके से सैंट्रल गवर्नमैंट या स्टेट गवर्नमैंट को इसको कंट्रोल करना चाहिए। It has to be controlled. Today the common man in our country is reeling under the adverse impact of price rise. Not only common man, but every upper middle class is also feeling the pinch of price rise. Of late, we notice that the prices of essential commodities like grains, pulses, vegetables etc. are going up very fast and on the other hand there is no appropriate increase in the income of our citizens. As a responsible Government, it is the responsibility of the Government to address the problem and bail out the people of this country from the clutches of price rise. प्राइस राइज़ तो हो रहा है, लेकिन हमारी जेब में पैसा नहीं बढ़ रहा है। Before we look at solutions to contain price rise of essential commodities we should know as to what are the reasons for this menace. In my view, productivity of foodgrains is not matching with the increasing demand of consumption. At the same time, we find depletion of cultivable lands due to developmental activities and mindless urbanization. Highly fertile lands are being used for non-agricultural purposes, irregular and unscientific cropping patterns are leading to fluctuating production of a particular commodity. 

Another major reason for price rise is hoarding of essential commodities by black marketers. Of course, natural calamities do contribute to price rise by affecting crop production. 

Sir, you know that my State is a two year old State. We are a newly born State. But my Chief Minister, Shri KCR, is very much concerned about the State and its people. 

I will now explain the steps taken by Telangana Government to control prices of essential commodities in Telangana. It has decided to supply tur dal, onions, etc. at subsidized rates by setting up special counters of Rythu Bazaars and other locations in the State. The Government has sought Rs. 25 crore from the Centre’s National Market Intervention Fund. Steps taken by our State Government are yielding good results and prices of essential commodities are being stabilised. Similar measures may be adopted by the Central Government to see that essential commodities prices are under control. 

Prices of life saving drugs should be made affordable for common people. आप तो जानते हैं कि आज कोई भी आदमी हॉस्पीटल जाने के नाम पर डरता है। आज अगर कोई मिडिल क्लास का आदमी एक बार हॉस्पीटल के अंदर चला जाए तो उसे यह टेस्ट, वह टेस्ट कह कर उसका बिल वहां पर मिनिमम एक लाख रुपए से लेकर पांच लाख रुपए तक हो जाता है। This has to be controlled. 

There are many pharmaceutical companies which are manufacturing generic drugs under their brand name and are charging manifold against production cost. For example, generic paracetamol will cost only ten paisa per tablet but branded paracetamol may cost upto Rs.20 or Rs. 25 or Rs. 30. At times, doctors prescribe only branded tablets even though cheap formulations are available. The Government should check these unethical alliances between doctors and pharma companies to save the common man from undue high price of essential drugs. There is a n need to bring in more transparency while fixing the ceiling price of life saving drugs.

The Government may invoke provision No. 19 of DPCO (Drug Price Control Order) 2013 to fix the ceiling price of life saving drugs as and when the need is felt. It pains to know that someone died due to high price of medicines which means that the man was killed by high price and not by the disease itself. इसको नोट करना चाहिए, क्योंकि आदमी जब अन्दर जाता है तो बेचारा परेशान होता है। परेशानी में उसे लगता है कि मेरा बिल कितना जा रहा है। How much bill have I to pay? वह परेशानी उसकी बीमारी से ज्यादा होती है। 

I request the Government to see that we have a strong policy in place to see that life saving medicines are timely available in adequate quantity at affordable prices. I would even say to this extent that if the Governments fails its citizens, it is a failing (or falling) Government. Therefore, in line with other hon. Members view, I urge upon this Government to act and act fast to save the common man from the ill effects of price rise.

As far as essential food commodities are concerned, I request that there should be strict action against hoarders; there should be adequate storage facilities to meet the exigencies. There should be initiatives to increase cultivable land on regular basis. Our R&D should concentrate on increasing productivity of food commodities. 

सर, अगर हम ये पूरे स्टेप्स प्रॉपर्ली लेंगे, we can really control the price rise instead of blaming other Parties. We have to see that the common man lives with a proper income and pricing. 

सर, आप मुझे ज्यादा बोलने नहीं दे रहे हैं।

, महंगाई निश्चित ही देश का एक बड़ा मुद्दा है । खाद्य पदार्थों के दामों में लगातार उतार-चढ़ाव बना हुआ है । आज चीजों के जो दाम बढ़े है उसका बड़ा कारण देश का बिगड़ता हुआ मानसून है । हालाकि यूपीए सरकार की तुलना में एसी चीजों के दामों में गिरावट आई है किन्तु मूल्यों की जो स्थिरता होनी चाहिए वह चिन्ता का वि­षय है । मांग एवं आपूर्ति का जब संतुलन बिगड़ता है तभी महंगाई बढ़ती है । आज देश में दालों का तथा तिलहन का उत्पादन कम हुआ हे । सब्जियों की महंगाई का कारण बिगड़ता मानसून है , लेकिन इन सबके बाद भी मुद्रास्फीति पूरी तरह से कंट्रोल में है, मूल्य दरों में व्यापक कमी आई है । भंडारण एक बड़ी आवश्यकता है । जिसकी कमी धीरे धीरे ही पूरी की जा सकती है । कभी प्याज 70 रूपये किलो बिकती थी, आज किसानों ने 5 रूपये किलो में बेचने के लिए मजबूर हुए है । इसके दो कारण हैं पहला उत्पादन की अधिकता तथ दूसरा भंडारण की कमी, ठीक इसी तरह टमाटर किसान को 2 रूपये किलो के भाव से मिलता है, लेकिन भंडारण तथा मौसम की गड़बड़ी के कारण बिचौलियों को दाम बढ़ाने का मौका मिल जाता है ।

महंगाई पर कंट्रोल कैसे हो, यह राज्य का वि­षय है । मुनाफागिरी पर रोक लगाने का काम जिस प्रभावी तरीके से होना चाहिए नहीं हो पा रहा है।

हमारी सरकार ने मांग एवं आपूर्ति को ध्यान में रखकर महंगाई को नियंत्रित किया है। सभी राज्यों को चाहिए कि सरकारी दुकानें जगह जगह खोले तथा आम आदमी को सस्ते दर पर सामान उपलब्ध कराये । इस दिशा में पहल करने की जरूरत है ।

वेजीटेबल के भंडारण हेतु नए उपाय की जरूरत है । दालों एवं तिलहन का उत्पादन बढ़ाने के लिए इस सीजन में सरकार ने जो प्रयास किये हैं इसके माध्यम से सार्थक परिणाम देखने को मिलेंगे । ।

पेट्रोलियम पदार्थों के लगातार दाम घटे हैं, गरीब की रसाई के लिए गैस चूल्हा देना इस बात का प्रमाण है कि आम आदमी की हर जरूरत को पूरा करने के लिए सरकार पूरी तरह से चिंतित है और कारगर उपाय कर रही है । पड़ोसी देशों के साथ भी जरूरत को पूरा करने हेतु बात-चीत लगातार की जा रही है। देश में पीडीएस सिस्टम पहले से बेहतर हो रहा है और गरीबों को सस्ती दर पर खाद्यान्न मिल रहा है, इन्हीं दुकानों के माध्यम से अन्य जरूरी चीजों का विक्रय कराने की जरूरत है। 

एक तरफ किसान का उचित दाम उसकी फसल का नहीं मिलता है । यह शिकायत है वहीं दूसरी तरफ आम उपभोक्ता को महंगे दर पर चीजें मिल रही है । इस विसंगति को दूर करने के लिए कुछ कारगर कदम उठाने की जरूरत है ।
